meta.title: GLP-1 Agonists Are Associated With a Significant Reduction in Breast Cancer Incidence in Women.
meta.abstract:
Purpose

Excess weight is a key modifiable risk factor for breast cancer. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1) promote weight loss and improve metabolic health, but their effect on breast cancer risk remains unclear.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective cohort study from January 1, 2022, to June 30, 2025, using electronic health records. We identified 217,624 unique women who underwent breast imaging; restricting to ages 45-80 years with a BMI ≥25 and a documented imaging outcome (n = 111,646; median age 61 years). The primary outcome was breast cancer detection. GLP-1 use was defined as a first prescription before the examination date and assessed in relation to race, ethnicity, age, and type 2 diabetes. To address potential confounding between these covariates and GLP-1 exposure, we performed one-to-one, case-control matching using propensity scores on the basis of age, race, ethnicity, highest BMI, breast density, and history of type 2 diabetes. The propensity matching to the GLP-1 use group was performed using the greedy nearest neighbor approach.

Results

GLP-1 exposure was associated with a lower incidence of breast cancer (odds ratio [OR], 0.649 [95% CI, 0.569 to 0.741]; P < .0001). In the matched logistic regression (30,528 observations; 600 cancer cases), GLP-1 exposure was associated with a lower breast cancer incidence (OR, 0.695 [95% CI, 0.590 to 0.819]; P < .0001).

Conclusion

In this large observational study of women undergoing breast imaging at a major academic center and affiliated sites, GLP-1 treatment was associated with a lower incidence of breast cancer, independent of age, race, ethnicity, BMI, breast density, and diabetes. The findings support the need for prospective trials investigating GLP-1 agonists for breast cancer prevention.

domains.name: Confounding
domains.direction_justification: In the matched dataset (Table A2), matched non-users had a higher baseline rate of prior breast cancer history (7.8%, n=1,197) compared to GLP-1 users (5.9%, n=907), despite prior breast cancer being a major determinant of future breast cancer risk. Additionally, critical unmeasured confounders (family history, BRCA status, parity, exogenous hormone therapy, and alcohol use) were omitted from propensity score matching.

findings.mechanism: Prior personal history of breast cancer substantially elevates subsequent breast malignancy risk. Because the control group retained a higher prevalence of prior breast cancer (7.8% vs 5.9%), this baseline risk discrepancy artificially deflates the relative risk in the GLP-1 group.

domains.name: Measurement of the exposure
domains.direction_justification: Defining exposure as any single prescription before the imaging examination date without a required minimum duration or latency allows patients with very short, biologically implausible exposure windows to be categorized as protected, introducing immortal time and reverse causality biases.

findings.title: Absence of latency, minimum duration, and dose-response criteria
findings.mechanism: Solid tumor carcinogenesis requires years to develop or prevent. Classifying individuals who received a single prescription shortly before mammography as 'exposed' cannot reflect a true biological preventative mechanism and distorts the association.
evidence: Methods (page 1342): 'GLP-1 agonist use was defined as a first prescription before the examination date'.
Discussion (page 1347): 'we did not specifically examine the impact of exposure duration or drug dosage on cancer development. We also did not require a minimum duration of therapy'.

findings.title: Exposure ascertainment error from EHR prescription records
findings.mechanism: Prescription orders in EHR do not confirm medication dispensing, adherence, or out-of-system/compounding pharmacy GLP-1 acquisition.
evidence: Discussion (page 1347): 'there could be patients on GLP-1 agonists who obtained these drugs outside of our health system, including non-FDA-approved doses and formulations at compounding pharmacies'.

findings.title: Absence of Lag Period in a Short Study Window
findings.mechanism: A cancer detected shortly after a prescription predates drug initiation. Failing to discard early follow-up attributes pre-existing subclinical tumor absence or presence to recent exposure.
evidence: We also did not require a minimum duration of therapy, because exposure is not definitely related to dose
we did not specifically examine the impact of exposure duration or drug dosage on cancer development.

findings.title: Prevalent-User and Ever-Use Misclassification
findings.mechanism: Classifying exposure as any prescription prior to the outcome examination without a new-user cohort or washout introduces depletion of susceptibles and survivor bias.
evidence: GLP-1 agonist use was defined as a first prescription before the examination date
reduction in breast cancer diagnoses within the study group associated with any prior or current use of GLP-1 agonist.

findings.title: Immortal Time Window Between First Prescription and Imaging
findings.mechanism: Requiring a prescription prior to an imaging exam without alignment of cohort entry creates an unaddressed interval where patients in the exposed group could not have had an imaging-confirmed event.
evidence: GLP-1 agonist use was defined as a first prescription before the examination date

domains.name: Selection of participants into the study
domains.direction_justification: Conditioning cohort entry on undergoing breast imaging between 2022 and 2025 creates collider stratification bias and immortal time bias, because GLP-1 users had to survive cancer-free up to their prescription date prior to imaging.

findings.title: Conditioning on breast imaging examination (collider bias)
findings.mechanism: Selecting participants from women who presented for breast imaging inside a single health system selects on health-seeking behavior and surveillance frequency, which correlates with GLP-1 prescribing and cancer detection.
evidence: Methods (page 1341, 1343): Initial cohort identified as 217,624 unique women who underwent breast imaging between January 1, 2022, and June 30, 2025.
Table 1: True positive rates were 2.4% (2,295/96,382) in unexposed vs 1.6% (241/15,264) in exposed.

findings.title: Immortal time bias in retrospective cohort definition
findings.mechanism: Exposure defined as receiving a prescription prior to an imaging exam within an arbitrary fixed calendar window requires patients to remain alive and cancer-free until drug initiation.
evidence: Study schema (Fig 1) and methods define the study period from January 1, 2022, to June 30, 2025, matching post-hoc without prospective person-time alignment from drug initiation.

domains.name: Post-exposure interventions
domains.direction_justification: Differential use of other antidiabetic therapies (e.g., metformin, insulin, sulfonylureas) or concurrent weight loss interventions during follow-up was unmeasured and could push estimates in either direction.

findings.title: Unmeasured concurrent metabolic medications and interventions
findings.mechanism: Concomitant alterations in diabetes and weight-loss management regimens after GLP-1 initiation may modulate breast cancer risk independently.
evidence: Table 1 shows 53.4% of GLP-1 users had type 2 diabetes versus 17.6% of non-GLP-1 users in the overall cohort, but post-index co-medication trajectories were unadjusted.

domains.name: Missing data
domains.direction_justification: Exclusion of 54,799 women due to BMI <25 or missing/unrecorded BMI, plus loss of cancer events occurring outside the Penn Medicine EHR network, could bias results in either direction depending on differential out-of-system migration.

findings.title: Out-of-system outcome and exposure attrition
findings.mechanism: EHR-based data extraction cannot capture imaging or malignant diagnoses performed at outside health centers.
evidence: Figure 1: 54,799 women excluded for BMI <25 or lack of qualifying records; 14.7% (16,451/111,646) lacked mammographic density data due to ultrasound/MRI modality.

domains.name: Measurement of the outcome
domains.direction_justification: Pathology-confirmed malignant breast diagnosis is objective and reliable; slight non-differential under-ascertainment of outside diagnoses tends to attenuate risk differences towards the null.

findings.title: Objective pathological outcome definition
findings.mechanism: Malignant breast pathology diagnoses documented within the EHR represent standardized and validated endpoints with low risk of diagnostic misclassification.
evidence: Methods (page 1342): 'The primary outcome was a malignant breast pathology diagnosis during the study period'.

domains.name: Selection of the reported result
domains.direction_justification: Reporting a single observational propensity-matched model without a registered pre-analysis plan or sensitivity analyses addressing exposure duration, latency gaps, or exclusion of prior cancer cases biases findings toward statistically significant protective associations.

findings.title: Omission of sensitivity analyses on exposure latency and prior malignancy
findings.mechanism: The study does not report essential sensitivity analyses (e.g., restricted to incident drug users, requiring >=1-2 years latency, or excluding patients with a history of breast cancer), which are standard to verify non-spurious protective effects.
evidence: Table 3 and Table 4 report overall unmatched (OR 0.649) and matched (OR 0.695) models only, without lagged or duration-stratified models.

overall.summary: The study exhibits a high overall risk of bias predominantly driven by exposure misclassification (no latency period or minimum exposure duration required), immortal time bias, selection conditioning on breast imaging attendance, and residual confounding (notably an imbalance in prior breast cancer history in the matched cohort: 7.8% in controls vs 5.9% in GLP-1 users). These design flaws systematically exaggerate the apparent protective association between GLP-1 agonist use and breast cancer incidence away from the null.

unresolvable_without_more_data: Medication adherence, cumulative dose, and treatment duration (dispensation/claims data required).
Exposure latency and lag-time analyses (time-to-event data from drug initiation required).
Reproductive risk factors, family history of breast cancer, and genetic mutation status.
Out-of-system cancer diagnoses and prescription fills from outside health systems/compounding pharmacies.

baseline_comparability.summary: Although the GLP-1 exposed cohort had higher metabolic comorbidity and BMI at baseline, the matched comparison failed to control for prior breast cancer history, which was substantially higher among unexposed controls (7.8% vs 5.9%).
